title: Pansutong tasks.json
description: Pansutong Document JSON. Desktop now persists this document per-device as a SQLite database (tasks_<device>.db); this JSON shape is the legacy on-disk format still used for one-time migration/import, the Android SAF sync wire format, and export. Settings are device-local in config.json and are not part of this document.

version.description: Document schema version. Missing versions load as the current app version. Version 4+ stores timestamps as ISO-8601 strings; version 5+ stores reusable templates in a separate template_tasks list instead of as is_template tasks; version 6+ records per-task time-tracking entries in time_entries; version 7+ records template recurrence; version 8+ records multi-day recurrence shapes; version 9+ records per-device merge tombstones and tag updated_at; version 10+ records task and template attachment metadata.

last_modified.description: Last task, template task, or tag edit, as an ISO-8601 timestamp in local time with an offset (e.g. 2026-06-01T20:34:56+08:00). Legacy files may store integer epoch milliseconds or a UTC 'Z' timestamp; older files may omit it, loading as 0.

tags.description: Flat tags. Tasks reference tags by id; tags do not own task membership.

tasks.description: Ordinary tasks. Reusable task blueprints live in template_tasks, not in this list.

template_tasks.description: Reusable task blueprints. Template tasks are independent objects and are not active tasks.

deleted_tasks.description: Delete tombstones for tasks, used by per-device replica merging.

deleted_tags.description: Delete tombstones for tags, used by per-device replica merging.

deleted_template_tasks.description: Delete tombstones for template tasks, used by per-device replica merging.

deleted_attachments.description: Delete tombstones for attachments, used by per-device replica merging so attachment deletes propagate across devices.

timestamp.description: A point in time. Written as an ISO-8601 timestamp in local time with an offset at second precision (e.g. 2026-06-01T20:34:56+08:00); legacy files may store a UTC 'Z' timestamp or a non-negative integer count of epoch milliseconds. All forms load (the offset keeps the instant unambiguous).

tagId.description: Tag identifier. New app-created tags use t_ followed by 12 hex characters.

taskId.description: Task identifier. New app-created tasks use k_ followed by 12 hex characters.

timeEntry.description: One time-tracking session on a task (#81). An entry without an 'end' is the running timer (open interval); closed entries are finished sessions.

id.description: Time-entry identifier. New app-created entries use te_ followed by 12 hex characters.

end.description: When the session ended. Null and missing both mean the timer is still running.

attachment.description: Metadata for a managed file attachment stored beside the per-device tasks replica. The path is a relative managed filename, never an absolute path.

id.description: Attachment identifier. New app-created attachments use att_ followed by 12 hex characters.

path.description: Managed relative filename in the data folder.

priority.description: Priority weight. A task's effective priority is the max weight among its tags; missing priority loads as 0.

pinned.description: Whether this tag is pinned to the sidebar. Missing pinned loads as false.

updated_at.description: Last tag edit, as an ISO-8601 local-time timestamp with an offset. Omitted or 0 for tags written before this field existed.

due_date.description: Due date. Null and missing both load as no due date.

start_date.description: Start date. Null and missing both load as no start date. Legacy files' scheduled_date is accepted as an alias on load.

start_time.description: Optional time-of-day for start_date, 'HH:MM' local. Absent = all-day. Legacy files' scheduled_time is accepted as an alias on load.

due_time.description: Optional time-of-day for due_date, 'HH:MM' local. Absent = all-day.

notes.description: Free-form notes. Missing notes load as an empty string.

attachments.description: Managed file attachments shown with the task notes. Attachment bytes live beside the per-device tasks replica.

tag_ids.description: Tag ids attached to this task. Untagged tasks are Inbox tasks.

estimated_seconds.description: Estimated effort for this task in whole seconds. Null and missing both mean no estimate.

completed_at.description: When the task was completed, as an ISO-8601 local-time timestamp with an offset (legacy files may store a UTC 'Z' timestamp or epoch milliseconds). Null and missing both load as incomplete.

updated_at.description: Last task edit, as an ISO-8601 local-time timestamp with an offset (legacy files may store a UTC 'Z' timestamp or epoch milliseconds). Omitted or 0 for tasks written before this field existed.

time_entries.description: Recorded time-tracking sessions (#81). Omitted for tasks with no tracked time. An entry without an 'end' is the running timer.

recurrence.description: Template recurrence schedule. This schema describes the current v8 serialized shape.

notes.description: Free-form notes copied to spawned tasks. Missing notes load as an empty string.

attachments.description: Managed file attachments copied to spawned tasks with the template notes.

tag_ids.description: Tag ids copied to spawned tasks.

updated_at.description: Last template edit, as an ISO-8601 local-time timestamp with an offset (legacy files may store a UTC 'Z' timestamp or epoch milliseconds). Omitted or 0 for templates written before this field existed.

due_offset_days.description: Spawned task due date offset from today. Null and missing both mean no due date.

start_offset_days.description: Spawned task start date offset from today. Null and missing both mean no start date. Legacy files' scheduled_offset_days is accepted as an alias on load.

estimated_seconds.description: Estimated effort copied to spawned tasks, in whole seconds. Null and missing both mean no estimate.

recurrence.description: Optional recurrence schedule. Null and missing both mean manual-only.

recurrence_tag_id.description: Tag id used for recurrence ghost suppression. Null and missing both mean unset.
